material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Blocking Primer for Wood/Engineered Trim

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
primer.notes: Standard acrylic primer for spot-priming bare areas on wood and engineered wood trim. Also used for full prime on failing/peeling states (>30% bare) on STANDARD softwood species (pine, fir, spruce). For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood), use SYS_EXT_TRRP_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK instead. Trim coverage slightly higher than siding due to smooth, non-porous profiles (PCA P10 one-foot rule: 1 SF per 1 LF).

applies_when.condition: bare areas exposed AND wood_chemistry != tannin_rich

material_systems.notes: Primary primer for wood and engineered wood trim. Spot prime on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (bare spots only). Spot or full prime on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT depending on bare percentage. Full prime on SS_EXT_PEELING. For engineered wood, also seal all field-cut edges before priming (separate edge sealer product).

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer for Tannin-Rich Wood

products: KILZ Original Multi-Surface Stain Blocking Primer
primer.notes: REQUIRED for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood) when bare wood is exposed. Oil-based provides superior tannin bleed block vs acrylic. Longer dry time — 24 hr recoat in cool weather. VOC restrictions may apply in some jurisdictions. On trim, coverage is per affected bare area using PCA P10 one-foot rule.

applies_when.condition: bare wood exposed (scraped areas on cedar/redwood trim)

material_systems.notes: Tannin-rich species override. When cedar or redwood bare wood is exposed during scraping, this system REPLACES the acrylic primer. Higher material consumption due to absorptive open grain on tannin-rich species. Latex primer on bare cedar/redwood WILL bleed — alkyd is non-negotiable.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for PVC Trim

primer.type: Bonding primer / adhesion promoter for non-porous substrates
products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Stix Bonding Primer
primer.notes: REQUIRED for cellular PVC trim (AZEK, VERSATEX) when bare areas are exposed during prep. PVC is non-porous — standard acrylic and alkyd primers will NOT adhere. Scuff-sand with 220-grit before applying bonding primer. Higher coverage than wood primers because PVC is non-absorptive.

applies_when.condition: bare PVC exposed at scraped areas

material_systems.notes: PVC substrate override. Standard latex primer will not adhere to PVC — peeling sheets within 6-12 months. Bonding primer provides mechanical grip on non-porous plastic surface. Must scuff-sand glossy PVC with 220-grit before application.

material_systems.name: Chalk-Binding Conditioner Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Multi-Purpose Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for chalking surfaces regardless of substrate material. Low-viscosity, high-penetration formula binds loose chalk residue and creates sound adhesion base. Must apply after power wash cleaning and 24-48 hour drying. Higher material consumption than standard primer — chalk residue absorbs aggressively. Heavy chalk = lower end of coverage range.

material_systems.notes: REQUIRED for chalking surfaces. Penetrates and binds loose chalk particles. Do NOT skip — topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Applies to all substrate materials (wood, PVC, engineered) in chalking state. Full-surface application required.

material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Trim Finish

finish.notes: Standard and premium trim finish. QT3 uses production-grade 100% acrylic. QT4 uses premium acrylic or acrylic-urethane blend for enhanced durability and flow. 2 coats required at both tiers. Trim coverage is higher than siding — smooth profiles on primed/previously coated surface. PCA P10 one-foot rule for trim: 1 SF per 1 LF.

material_systems.notes: Primary finish system for exterior trim repaint. QT3 satin is standard exterior trim sheen. QT4 semi-gloss accentuates architectural detail — requires thorough prep (semi-gloss reveals every imperfection). QT4 permits acrylic-urethane blend for superior flow and durability.

material_systems.name: Solar-Reflective Finish for PVC Trim (LRV <55)

products: Benjamin Moore Regal Select Exterior (Colors for Vinyl)
finish.notes: REQUIRED when substrate_material = PVC AND selected color LRV < 55. Solar-reflective pigment technology reduces heat absorption to prevent PVC thermal distortion (warping, buckling, joint opening). Standard dark-color paints on PVC cause excessive heat buildup. Slightly lower coverage than standard trim finish due to reflective pigment loading.

material_systems.notes: Gate condition: PVC trim with dark colors (LRV <55) MUST use solar-reflective coating. Standard paint voids PVC warranty and causes thermal distortion. If LRV >=55, use standard SYS_EXT_TRRP_FINISH_ACRYLIC instead. Document color approval before ordering.

spot_prime_area.notes: Coverage based on affected bare area, not total trim LF. PCA P10: 1 SF per 1 LF of affected trim. Typical bare percentage: 5-15% on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, 15-30% on mild SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.

assumptions: Coverage applies to affected area only — not full component LF.
Bare percentage determined during condition assessment.
PVC (bonding primer) has slightly higher coverage than wood (acrylic) due to non-porous surface.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Full prime on failing state (>30% bare) for standard softwoods. Mixed surface — some bare wood, some existing coating. Trim profiles are smooth — better coverage than rough siding.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Full prime on peeling state — mostly bare after heavy scraping. Standard softwoods. Slightly lower coverage due to exposed grain.

assumptions: Full-surface prime required when bare percentage >= 30% or state is SS_EXT_PEELING.
PCA P10 one-foot rule: trim < 12 inches wide = 1 SF per 1 LF.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Alkyd stain-block on tannin-rich wood (cedar, redwood). Lower coverage than acrylic — tannin-rich open grain absorbs more primer.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Alkyd stain-block on extensively bare tannin-rich wood. Highest primer consumption in this spec.

assumptions: Alkyd coverage 15-20% lower than acrylic due to tannin-rich wood absorption.
Tannin-rich species: cedar, redwood. All other softwoods use acrylic primer.

SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.notes: Bonding primer on PVC trim. Non-porous surface = highest coverage. Apply to all bare PVC areas after scuff sanding.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Bonding primer on PVC trim peeling state. Non-porous surface coverage is consistent regardless of state severity.

assumptions: PVC is non-porous — coverage is consistent across substrate states.
Must scuff-sand PVC with 220-grit before bonding primer application.

SS_EXT_CHALKING.notes: Full-surface chalk-binding primer. Chalk residue absorbs significant primer. Heavy chalk (south/west facing fascia and rake) = lower end of range. Light chalk = upper end.

assumptions: Full-surface coverage required — chalk binding must be uniform.
Power wash first to remove loose chalk; primer binds remaining residue.
Applies to all substrate materials (wood, PVC, engineered) in chalking state.

simple_flat.notes: Flat board trim (1x4, 1x6 fascia, flat casing). Best coverage — smooth surface, no profile detail. PCA P10: 1 SF per 1 LF.

standard_profiled.notes: Single-piece profiled trim (clamshell, ogee). Slightly higher material use in profile grooves.

built_up.notes: Multi-piece assembly (2-piece crown, window surround with header cap). Multiple edges and joints increase material consumption.

elaborate.notes: Complex multi-piece with decorative elements (dentil, returns, pilasters). Highest material consumption due to intricate detail surfaces.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET trim area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_EDGE_LF.* keys, using PCA P10 one-foot rule).
Repaint coverage slightly higher than NC — primed/existing paint reduces absorption on intact areas.
2-coat system standard at QT3/QT4/QT5. No single-coat option — trim is fine-finish substrate.
Solar-reflective finish (IR) has ~5% lower coverage than standard acrylic due to reflective pigment loading.
Waste factor +15% per PCA P10 for trim (higher waste than field surfaces due to small-area brush application).

consumables.name: Angled sash brush 2-3 inch
consumables.notes: Primary applicator for exterior trim. 2 inch for narrow profiles and detail, 2.5-3 inch for fascia and wide flat trim. Angled sash for clean lines at trim-to-siding junctions. Quality brush is critical for trim finish — nylon/polyester blend for acrylic exterior coatings.

consumables.name: Airless spray tips 311-413 (fine trim pattern)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. 311 for narrow trim profiles, 413 for wider fascia/band board. Fine fan pattern for trim detail — smaller tip than siding. Faster tip wear at narrow orifices.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter for latex
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. Standard 60-mesh filter for latex exterior coatings. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: Carbide scrapers (rigid and flexible)
consumables.notes: For removing loose and peeling paint from trim profiles. Carbide stays sharp longer than steel. Rigid for flat surfaces, flexible for profiled trim. CONDITIONAL: substrate_state = SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT or SS_EXT_PEELING.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 80-120 grit (scraping/feathering)
consumables.notes: For feather-edge sanding at ALL scraped areas. 80 grit for heavy paint buildup feathering, 120 grit for standard feather-edge work. Feather sanding is MANDATORY whenever scraping occurs — non-negotiable at all quality tiers.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-180 grit (interstage/adhesion)
consumables.notes: For interstage sanding between coats at QT4/QT5 and adhesion tooth on sound existing paint. 150 grit between finish coats (QT4). 180 grit for light scuff on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT prep.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit (PVC scuff / QT5 final sand)
consumables.notes: For scuff-sanding glossy PVC trim before bonding primer (CONDITIONAL: substrate_material = pvc). Also for QT5 final interstage sand before topcoat.

consumables.name: Tack cloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Remove sanding dust before prime or finish coat. Critical at QT4/QT5 where dust nibs are visible in semi-gloss/gloss finish.

consumables.name: TSP cleaner / degreaser
consumables.notes: Trisodium phosphate or TSP substitute for surface cleaning before painting. Mix per manufacturer directions. Used during power wash prep step.

consumables.name: Wire brush for rust spots and stubborn deposits
consumables.notes: For removing rust stains from nail heads, hardware, and flashing contact areas on trim. Also for stubborn chalk deposits resistant to washing.

consumables.name: Solvent-based polymer exterior caulk (NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad)
consumables.notes: Primary caulk for all trim substrates. Solvent-based polymer or polyurethane formulation. Paintable. Compatible with wood, PVC, and engineered wood. NEVER use silicone — silicone prevents paint adhesion and is incompatible with PVC. Per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol: SEAL corner joints, trim-to-siding gaps, casing joints. NEVER SEAL weep holes, bottom overlaps, metal-to-wood flashing.

consumables.name: Caulk gun (dripless ratchet type)
consumables.notes: Dripless ratchet-type caulk gun for clean bead application. Standard tool — reusable.

consumables.name: Penetrating edge sealer for engineered wood
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: substrate_material = engineered_wood. Penetrating resin sealer for all field-cut edges on LP SmartSide and similar engineered trim. Prevents irreversible edge swelling from moisture absorption. NOT the same as spot primer — this is a specialized edge treatment. Warranty requirement.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. Used for glass edge masking (brush method), fixture protection, roofline edge protection.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper 12-18 inch
consumables.notes: For masking windows, doors, and siding adjacent to trim during spray application. CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. Also used for roofline edge protection (shingles/flashing).

consumables.name: Masking film with tape edge (pre-taped poly)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: application_method = spray. Pre-taped plastic film for full window and door masking during spray application. Faster than paper/tape combo for large masking areas.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.notes: For landscape and hardscape protection from scraping debris, wash water, and paint drips/overspray. Minimum 4 mil for durability. Scraping generates paint chips requiring containment.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Reusable canvas drops along foundation/walkway at base of trim work area. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Catches drips, scraping debris, and wash water.

consumables.name: Lead test kits (EPA-recognized)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true. EPA-recognized test kits (e.g., 3M LeadCheck). Required before disturbing paint on pre-1978 structures. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint — historically trim received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces.

consumables.name: Polyethylene sheeting 6 mil (RRP containment)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP rule. Heavier gauge than standard protection — must contain lead paint debris.

consumables.name: HEPA vacuum bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. For HEPA vacuum during and after lead-safe scraping. Required throughout prep phase when lead is present.

consumables.name: Lead-safe waste disposal bags
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil bags for lead paint waste. Labeled per EPA requirements.

consumables.name: P100 respirator cartridges
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. P100 particulate filter for half-face respirator during lead paint disturbance.

consumables.name: Disposable coveralls (Tyvek)
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. Disposable coveralls prevent lead dust transfer. Required for all crew during lead paint disturbance.

ext_siding_mask.description: Siding adjacent to trim — mask during spray application
ext_siding_mask.notes: Paper/film and tape along trim-siding junction during spray. Not needed for brush — brush work on trim does not generate overspray onto siding.

ext_window_mask.description: Window glass masking when painting window casings
ext_window_mask.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
ext_window_mask.notes: Brush: tape at glass edge only. Spray: full glass masking with paper/film.

ext_door_mask.description: Door face/glass masking when painting door casings
ext_door_mask.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
ext_door_mask.notes: Brush: tape at casing-door junction. Spray: full door face cover.

ext_ground_cover.description: Landscape and ground protection from scraping debris, wash water, and paint drips
ext_ground_cover.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray or when scraping generates debris
ext_ground_cover.notes: Canvas drops at base of work area. Scraping generates paint chips requiring containment — active during prep phase AND coating phase. RRP adds 10-ft containment perimeter with 6-mil poly.

ext_hardscape_protection.description: Walkway and patio surfaces below trim work areas
ext_hardscape_protection.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when scraping or spray generates debris
ext_hardscape_protection.notes: Drop cloth runners on walkways and patios. Paint chips from scraping and wash water contain old coating material.

ext_roofline_protection.description: Roofing material protection when painting fascia and rake
ext_roofline_protection.notes: Tape and paper at roofline edge. Protect shingles and flashing from drips. Paint drips on asphalt shingles are difficult to remove.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to trim
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture. Common on fascia, casing, and corner boards.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, wood/engineered — spot prime bare areas only
compatibility_rules.notes: Existing paint is sound. Spot-prime bare areas from minor scraping/sanding only. No full prime needed if adhesion test passes.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint, PVC — spot prime with bonding primer
compatibility_rules.notes: PVC requires bonding primer even for spot priming. Standard acrylic primer will not adhere.
MANDATORY. Topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Applies to all substrate materials.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint <30% bare, standard wood — spot acrylic prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Minor failure on standard softwoods. Spot-prime scraped areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint <30% bare, tannin-rich wood — spot alkyd stain-block
compatibility_rules.notes: Tannin-rich override. Cedar/redwood bare exposure requires alkyd stain-blocker even for spot priming.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint <30% bare, PVC — spot bonding prime
compatibility_rules.notes: PVC substrate override. Bonding primer on all bare PVC areas after scuff sanding.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare, standard wood — full acrylic prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Extensive bare exposure on standard softwoods requires full prime.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare, tannin-rich wood — full alkyd stain-block
compatibility_rules.notes: Tannin-rich override for extensive failure. Cedar/redwood bare exposure requires alkyd stain-blocker.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing paint >=30% bare, PVC — full bonding prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Full bonding primer on extensively failing PVC trim.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling, standard wood — full acrylic prime
compatibility_rules.notes: Peeling = extensive bare after heavy scraping. Full prime required.

compatibility_rules.description: Peeling, tannin-rich wood — full alkyd stain-block

compatibility_rules.notes: Full bonding primer on peeling PVC trim.

compatibility_rules.description: PVC trim with LRV <55 — solar-reflective finish required
compatibility_rules.notes: GATE CONDITION. Standard dark paint on PVC causes thermal distortion. Solar-reflective coating is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Voids PVC warranty without it.

compatibility_rules.description: PVC trim with LRV >=55 or non-PVC — standard acrylic finish
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard finish for all non-PVC substrates AND PVC with light colors (LRV >=55).
Silicone lacks compatibility with PVC — will fail adhesion. Prevents future paint adhesion. Use NPC Solar Seal #900, OSI Quad, or polyurethane sealant.

then.reason: Structural damage (rot) outside painting scope. Refer to carpenter/contractor.

compatibility_rules.notes: Soft, punky, or structurally compromised trim cannot be painted. Requires replacement first. After repair, new material enters spec as SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.
QT5 (gloss) requires 2-coat primer system with interstage sanding between all coats (primer-to-primer, primer-to-finish, finish-to-finish). 4 total coating passes.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance — RRP supplies required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745) requires lead-safe work practices for pre-1978 homes when disturbing >2 SF on building exterior or >20 SF total. Trim is HIGH RISK for lead paint.

risk_notes.risk: Wood trim rot concentrated at horizontal surfaces (sills, fascia-to-rake junction, bottom of corner boards) where water pools. Painting over rot is cosmetic-only and fails within one season.
risk_notes.mitigation: Condition assessment with rot probe at vulnerable joints. Flag and exclude rotted areas from LF totals. Rot repair = carpentry scope.

risk_notes.topic: PVC adhesion failure from wrong primer
risk_notes.risk: Standard acrylic or alkyd primer on PVC trim peels in sheets within 6-12 months. Also fails when LRV <55 dark colors cause thermal cycling beyond PVC expansion limits.
risk_notes.mitigation: Identify PVC during assessment. Use bonding primer only. Check LRV before color approval. Solar-reflective coating for dark colors.

risk_notes.risk: Cedar and redwood contain water-soluble extractives that bleed through latex coatings as brown/yellow stains when bare wood is exposed.
risk_notes.mitigation: Alkyd stain-blocking primer mandatory on tannin-rich species when bare wood is exposed. Latex primer on bare cedar/redwood WILL bleed.

risk_notes.risk: Failed caulk allows water entry behind paint film, causing peeling, rot, and substrate damage. Most common cause of premature trim coating failure.
risk_notes.mitigation: Replace all failed caulk during prep. Use substrate-compatible sealant. NEVER silicone on PVC. Test adhesion of new caulk to old substrate.

risk_notes.risk: LP SmartSide and similar products swell irreversibly when field-cut edges are not sealed. Moisture absorbs at unprotected edges.
risk_notes.mitigation: Seal every field-cut edge with penetrating edge sealer. Inspect existing cut edges during assessment — swelling indicates prior improper installation (carpenter scope).

risk_notes.risk: Trim historically received oil-based lead paint more frequently than field surfaces. HIGH RISK surface for lead. Scraping without RRP containment disperses lead dust.
risk_notes.mitigation: Test all pre-1978 trim before any paint disturbance. Full RRP containment, wet scraping, HEPA vacuum, lead-safe disposal when lead is present.

risk_notes.risk: Decades of repainting without stripping creates excessive paint buildup. Deep cracks perpendicular to wood grain indicate reduced flexibility. Common on south/west-facing fascia and sills.
risk_notes.mitigation: Detect during condition assessment. May escalate to SC_SEVERE_DETERIORATION prep level. Partial or full strip may be required.

material_quantity_notes.waste_factor: +15% per PCA P10 for trim. Trim has higher waste than field surfaces due to small-area brush application and frequent container changes.
material_quantity_notes.pca_p10_one_foot_rule: Trim with girth < 12 inches: 1 SF per 1 LF. All coverage rates expressed per SF, all measurement inputs in LF — engine converts via one-foot rule.
material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: When application_method = spray: multiply material quantity by 1.25-1.33 for 50-70% transfer efficiency. Trim spray waste is higher than siding due to small target width and overspray beyond trim edges.
material_quantity_notes.two_coat_standard: 2 finish coats at all quality tiers (QT3/QT4/QT5). No single-coat option — trim is fine-finish substrate. QT5 adds 2-coat primer (4 total coating passes).
material_quantity_notes.profile_complexity_material: Built-up and elaborate profiles consume more material than flat profiles due to increased effective surface area in profile grooves, joints, and decorative elements.

assumptions.value: 325-425 SF/gal for acrylic primer on trim vs 300-400 SF/gal on siding
assumptions.source: Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md §Production Rates; PCA P10 one-foot rule
assumptions.note: Trim profiles are smoother and less porous than siding field surfaces. Previously coated trim absorbs less primer than rough-sawn siding.

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal — highest coverage of any primer in this spec
assumptions.note: PVC is non-porous — primer sits on surface rather than absorbing. Consistent coverage regardless of state severity.

assumptions.value: 325-425 SF/gal — approximately 5% lower coverage than standard acrylic
assumptions.source: Product data sheets for VinylSafe/Colors for Vinyl product lines
assumptions.note: No direct doctrine coverage for IR-reflective product coverage rates. Derived from manufacturer PDS data. Flag for field calibration.
Varies by joint width. Trim-to-siding joints are typically 1/4 inch — 30 LF/tube. Wider joints (corner boards, worn casing) may consume more.

assumptions.value: QT5 uses same finish products as QT4 (premium acrylic) but with 2-coat primer, interstage sanding, and gloss sheen
assumptions.note: QT5 difference is in process (more coats, interstage sand, flow additive for brush) not in product chemistry. Emerald-tier products permitted but not required.
